# "Problems of interest" run under hipblaslt-bench in the rocjitsu race-check
# sidecar (run_rocjitsu_hipblaslt_race_check.sh). One workload per line:
#
#   label | extra hipblaslt-bench arguments
#
# Each line's arguments are appended to a fixed base invocation
# (--initialization hpl --verify --iters 1 --cold_iters 0) and run under the
# rocjitsu race + logging plugins. Keep the set small and the sizes modest: this
# job runs on every hipBLASLt PR and executes entirely under CPU emulation, so
# runtime scales with m*n*k. Comment (#) and blank lines are ignored.
#
# label       | bench args
f32_nt_128    | --precision f32_r --transA N --transB T -m 128 -n 128 -k 128
f16_nn_128    | --precision f16_r --transA N --transB N -m 128 -n 128 -k 128
bf16_tn_128   | --precision bf16_r --transA T --transB N -m 128 -n 128 -k 128
#
# f8 GEMMs use an arch-dependent format: gfx942 (CDNA3) needs the FNUZ types
# (f8_fnuz_r/bf8_fnuz_r); OCP arches such as gfx950 use f8_r/bf8_r. This file is
# shared across race-check targets, so no single f8 row is portable. Enable a
# target-appropriate row once it is validated on that arch, e.g.:
#   f8_nt_128   | --precision f16_r --compute_input_typeA f8_fnuz_r --compute_input_typeB f8_fnuz_r --transA N --transB T -m 128 -n 128 -k 128   # gfx942
#   f8_nt_128   | --precision f16_r --compute_input_typeA f8_r --compute_input_typeB f8_r --transA N --transB T -m 128 -n 128 -k 128             # gfx950
